_howto: Curated answers for Ask my portfolio (/ask/). The page reads this file directly, so there is nothing to rebuild after editing it.

Each entry: q is a list of ways someone might ask (the first one is shown as a suggestion), a is the answer exactly as it should appear, link is where Read more goes (a path from the site root, or a full URL), status is published or draft.
Only published entries are shown. Drafts are a to-do list: write the answer in your own words, then change status to published.
Answers are shown word for word and never rewritten. The page also always shows the top passages from the site under an answer, so keep answers short.
Optional: source says where the facts came from, for your own reference. It is not shown.
No long dashes please: the page and its tests reject them.

q: What kind of work does she do?
answers.a: In her own words on the home page: "I work in the space between engineering, research, and design, building things that sense and respond to people. The discipline changes, the curiosity doesn't." Her focus areas there are applied ML, XR and spatial computing, HCI research, computer vision, data pipelines, human-centered design, and product design and prototyping.

q: What is this website made with?
What tech stack does the portfolio use?
How did she build her website?
Is this site built with React?
answers.a: It is a static site: hand-written HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript with no framework and no build step, hosted on GitHub Pages. The projects page reads assets/projects.json when it loads. The 3D VR headset in the home hero and the builder cube are three.js, scroll reveals use GSAP, and the physics in the hidden easter eggs (the 404 page, for one) is Matter.js. vr.html is an immersive WebXR version of the hero and featured work, also built with three.js. Lab models run on your own device with Transformers.js 4.3.0 or ONNX Runtime Web, on the GPU through WebGPU or on the CPU through WebAssembly, and stay cached after the first visit. The Study Lab subjects share one kit in lab/study/kit (kit.js, kit.css and a bundled three.js), where every chapter is a small module with a live demo, an explanation and a short check.
answers.source: Verified in the repo: CNAME, no package.json, assets/vr-headset.js and builder-cube.js (three@0.160.0), assets/timeline-scroll.js (gsap@3.12.5), assets/quake.js, 404.html and sticky-counter.html (matter-js@0.19.0), assets/vr-lobby.js (renderer.xr, immersive-vr), lab/models.json runtime (Transformers.js 4.3.0), lab/frame/engine.js (onnxruntime-web 1.30.0), lab/frame/device.js (WebGPU or WebAssembly), lab/study/kit/kit.js

q: What models are in the Lab?
answers.a: The Lab is where Rabiat tries new openly licensed ML models before building them into anything: what they can and can't do, and how they run on your own device. Nothing to install, nothing uploaded. The models that run in the browser say how big they are and where they will run before anything downloads, and stay on your device after the first visit. The ones too big for a browser link to a demo instead.

q: What can I learn on this site?
What subjects are in the Study Lab?
answers.a: The Study Lab is a set of hands on study labs, each built around one subject, among them machine learning (from regression to LLMs and agents), audio, circuits, VR and XR, design, physics, biology for pre-med, muscles on a 3D body, and the elements. Every chapter has a live demo, a plain words explanation, a going deeper part and a short check. Everything runs on your device and your scores stay in your browser.

Recent pieces include The Point Was to Learn (on rewarding learning instead of finished tasks, in AI and in people), Hands in Your Pockets (the Apple Watch as a touch surface), If AI Goes Dark (a language model that lives entirely on the phone) and Nobody Knows What The Last One Did (the AI deployment gap).

q: Can I see this site in VR?
Is there a VR version of the portfolio?
How do I view the site in a headset?
answers.a: Yes. vr.html is an immersive WebXR version of the home hero and featured work. Open it in a headset browser that supports WebXR, such as the Quest Browser, and tap Enter VR. On a laptop it opens as a 3D preview you can look around with the mouse.

q: How does Ask my portfolio work?
answers.a: It is search, not a chatbot. Every answer is either one Rabiat wrote herself or a passage quoted from the site, always with a link to where it came from, so it cannot make things up. Matching is BM25 keyword search with some synonyms, and it runs instantly in your browser. Smarter search optionally downloads a small search model from the Lab (mdbr-leaf-ir, about 23 MB) to rerank results by meaning, on your own device.
